requirements.text: Trust domains MUST be explicit and lower-trust input MUST NOT create authority.
Execution MUST follow the canonical lifecycle or an equivalent state-machine trace.
Semantic meaning MUST derive from an authoritative semantic contract.
Security- and meaning-relevant operations MUST have canonical graph identity.
Rewrites MUST preserve declared semantics under explicit algebraic preconditions.
Resolution MUST be deterministic or deterministically abstain on ambiguity.
Traversal MUST enforce semantic scope and bounded resource consumption.
Authorization MUST evaluate the fully resolved operation graph in trusted context.
Authorization provenance MUST bind semantics, policy, and validity to executable artifacts.
Planning MUST NOT widen authorized semantics.
Execution IR MUST be independently validated before crossing the provider boundary.
Provider execution MUST satisfy declared semantic and security fidelity requirements.
Mutation profiles MUST specify atomicity, idempotency, replay, concurrency, and failure behavior.
Plan caching MUST never substitute stale or broader authority for current authorization.
All transports and agents MUST converge on equivalent semantic and authorization behavior.
Semantic resource amplification MUST be bounded by enforceable budgets.
Evidence MUST reconstruct security lineage without becoming an authority source.
Generated metadata MUST be reproducible, version-bound, and semantically equivalent to its source.
Every normative requirement MUST map to independent validation and explicit conformance status.
Portable vectors MUST encode both successful and fail-closed expected outcomes.
Reference implementations MUST remain informative and disclose deviations from the normative standard.
